definition: Semantic parameterization is a conceptual modeling process for expressing natural language descriptions of a domain in first-order predicate logic.
details: The process yields a formalization of natural language sentences in Description Logic to answer the who, what and where questions in the Inquiry-Cycle Model (ICM) developed by Colin Potts and his colleagues at the Georgia Institute of Technology. The parameterization process complements the Knowledge Acquisition and autOmated Specification (KAOS) method, which formalizes answers to the when, why and how ICM questions in Temporal Logic, to complete the ICM formalization. The artifacts used in the parameterization process include a dictionary that aligns the domain lexicon with unique concepts, distinguishing between synonyms and polysemes, and several natural language patterns that aid in mapping common domain descriptions to formal specifications.

explainer.lead: Semantic parameterization turns plain-language descriptions of a domain into formal first-order predicate logic, giving analysts a rigorous specification instead of prose. It matters because it makes requirements machine-checkable and links natural language to formal methods.

tiers.eli5: It's like translating a written rulebook into a precise code that a computer can check, so nothing is left vague.
tiers.practitioner: Used to formalize natural-language requirements, typically alongside KAOS, which handles the when, why and how questions in Temporal Logic while parameterization covers who, what and where in Description Logic. A pitfall is that ambiguity in the original text must be resolved manually before formalization.
tiers.paperLevel: A conceptual modeling process that expresses natural language domain descriptions as first-order predicate logic, yielding Description Logic formalizations answering the who, what and where questions of the Inquiry-Cycle Model. It complements KAOS, which formalizes the when, why and how questions in Temporal Logic; it depends on careful manual interpretation of the source text.

explainer.example: A sentence like 'a customer places an order' is rewritten as a predicate-logic formula naming the agent and object, so it can be checked against a specification.
